function: Predictive beamforming for ISAC vehicular links: a CNN-LSTM-FCN network maps historical estimated channels directly to the beamforming matrix, minimizing CRBs under a sum-rate constraint (pp. 6-8).
system: RSU as dual-function radar-communication massive MIMO ULA, Nt = Nr = 32 antennas, K = 3 single-antenna vehicles, 30 GHz, LoS, no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: EPDnet: CNN encoders, LSTM predictors, FCN fusion and decoder; unsupervised offline training on a CRB-plus-penalty loss with Adam; pre-training transfer across vehicle counts (pp. 7-9, 12).
data_channel: Simulated LoS channel with three kinematic vehicle models (SLSV, SLSA, CLSV); 6000 training and 3000 test samples from Monte-Carlo; no standardized or measured channel (pp. 3-5, 9).
test_conditions: Same-simulator train/test sets (6000/3000 samples); model pre-trained on two vehicles, adapted to three vehicles in 10 epochs versus 32 from scratch (pp. 9, 12).
baselines: Non-learned: perfect beamforming (true angles, oracle), random beamforming. Learned: CLSTMnet [18], CNN-only, LSTM-only networks (pp. 9-10).
metrics: CRB of angle and distance (sensing), achievable sum-rate (communication), sensing-communication tradeoff, epochs to converge (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Big-O orders for CNN and LSTM units, offline training and online estimation of EPDnet and folded-EPDnet (Table II, p. 10); no FLOPs, parameter counts, or runtime.
q1_support: p. 3: "the communication channel is usually represented by a line-of-sight (LOS) channel model"
q2_support: p. 12: "the EPDnet with pre-training can quickly converge to a stable CRB value within 10 epochs, regardless of any changes in the number of vehicles"
q3_support: p. 10: "two schemes adopting CLSTMnet and the random beamforming method are considered as respective benchmarks for comparison"
q4_support: p. 9: "we will analyze the computational complexity of the proposed method for these two phases"
q5_support: p. 9: "The training set and test set consisted of 6000 and 3000 samples, respectively, generated by the Monte-Carlo method"
notes: Area 5: beamforming in an ISAC system. q1: custom LoS simulator with own kinematic models, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data. q2: Fig. 12 transfers a two-vehicle model to three vehicles (p. 12). q3: random and perfect (oracle) beamforming are non-learned; CLSTMnet [18] is an earlier learned predictive beamformer by overlapping authors. q4: Table II gives big-O orders only. q5: no code or data link.
